title: Mop sweeping hard floors
audience: Cleaners in any cleaning-group business who dry sweep hard floors and entry areas before a wet or vacuum pass.
learningOutcomes: Check a vacuum, dust pan and sweep mop head before use, including the vacuum's test label.
Sweep a floor edge first, then in figure-of-eight passes, without raising a dust cloud.
Remove chewing gum and sticky matter before sweeping, so the mop head is not contaminated.
Clean and store the mop head, dust pan and vacuum according to the colour system.
Stop and escalate when the floor is wet, slippery or contains an unidentified substance.

instruction.heading: What dry mop sweeping does and does not do
instruction.body: Dry mop sweeping lifts loose dust, grit and small debris from a floor without water. It is quick, and it suits large open areas and the first pass of a floor job. It works only while the mop head is clean and in full contact with the floor. Once a mop head is wet, greasy or full of debris, it spreads dirt instead of collecting it. Dry sweeping does not remove grease, marks or residue, which need a wet method under the approved procedure.

instruction.heading: Preparing before the first stroke
instruction.body: Check the vacuum you will use afterwards. Confirm its test label is valid, the plug is intact, the flex has no bare wires or tape, the bag is not full and the filter is clear. Use a clean mop head and a colour-coded dust pan and brush. Put on gloves before you touch the mop head, pick up large rubbish or check the vacuum bag and filter, because the source notes that chewing gum and rubbish can carry bacteria. Look at the floor for chewing gum and sticky patches first. Scrape gum up with a suitable tool into a refuse bag. A sticky mop head does not sweep effectively.

instruction.heading: The sweeping pattern
instruction.body: Start at the outside edges of the area and work along the walls so that dirt collects toward the middle. Then move to the point furthest from the door and sweep in figure-of-eight passes, working back toward the exit. Keep the mop head in contact with the floor, so dust is held rather than lifted into the air. Pause halfway through to check the mop head, and vacuum it if it is loaded. When the sweep is finished, vacuum the mop head and the floor around the area where it rested.

instruction.heading: Floor condition and safety while sweeping
instruction.body: A dry sweep should end with a floor that is free of debris, clean and dry, and not slippery. Do not sweep over a wet patch as though it were dry, because the mop will fail and the patch becomes a slip hazard. Sign-post any wet area, and make any trailing cable or open socket safe before you sweep near it. Take extra care when staff are still on the premises: keep the work area separated from people and do not sweep through them.

instruction.heading: After the sweep
instruction.body: Store mop heads head up in a holder, because heads stored face down collect dirt. Wash and dry dust pans, and store them by colour. Safety check and damp wipe the vacuum after use. Dispose of collected refuse in the designated waste area, and log any floor defect or hazard you found.

procedure: Check the vacuum's test label, plug, flex, bag and filter, and record any defect.
Fit a clean mop head and select the colour-coded dust pan and brush.
Put on gloves and scan the floor for chewing gum or sticky matter. Remove it into a refuse bag.
Sweep the outside edges first, working along the walls.
Sweep from the point furthest from the door in figure-of-eight passes, moving back toward the exit and keeping the head on the floor.
Halfway through, check the mop head and vacuum it if it is loaded.
Vacuum the mop head and the floor around it, then store the head up.
Wash the dust pan, wipe down the vacuum, and log any floor defect or hazard.

workedExamples.situation: In an office lobby you find a sticky patch by the door and a cardboard box of loose packaging.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What order do you work in?
workedExamples.reasoning: Put on gloves. Move the box and bulky packaging into a bag first, then scrape up the gum or sticky patch with a suitable tool. Only then sweep. Sweeping over the sticky patch contaminates the mop head and spreads the residue across the floor.

workedExamples.situation: Halfway through a sweep in a retail corridor, the mop head becomes wet from a spilled drink.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Stop, replace or clean the mop head, and deal with the spill using the approved wet method. A wet head no longer sweeps effectively and drags dirt about. Sign-post the wet area until it is dry.

equipmentAndPpe: Gloves for handling debris, chewing gum, bags, filters and the mop head.
Clean sweep mop head, in good condition, fitted to a holder.
Vacuum with a current test label.
Refuse bags for gum and large debris.

commonErrors.error: Sweeping over chewing gum with a dirty mop head.
commonErrors.prevention: Remove the gum first, then sweep with a clean head.

commonErrors.error: Sweeping in random strokes, which leaves dirt in the middle of the room.
commonErrors.prevention: Edges first, then figure-of-eight passes from the far point back toward the exit.

commonErrors.error: Lifting the mop off the floor, which creates a dust cloud.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the mop head in contact with the floor throughout the pass.

commonErrors.error: Storing the mop head face down in a bucket.
commonErrors.prevention: Store the head up in a holder.

commonErrors.error: Using a vacuum with a full bag or a blocked filter.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the bag and filter before switching the vacuum on.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The source requires gloves when lifting large rubbish and chewing gum, because these may carry bacteria, and when checking the vacuum bag and filter.
Trip and slip hazards: sign-post wet areas and make trailing cables and open sockets safe before sweeping.
Dust: avoid creating dust clouds. If the area has a known allergen, a dust-control instruction or a product on site, check its SDS before sweeping.
Electrical equipment: the vacuum checks in “Safe use and care of electrical machines” apply in full before and after use.

qualityStandard: Floor free of visible debris and chewing gum after the sweep.
No dust cloud produced during the sweep, as observed by the assessor.
Sweep pattern follows the edges-first, figure-of-eight method from the far point toward the exit.
Mop head clean at the start and checked halfway through.
Vacuum test label valid and checked before use.
documentationEvidence: Pre-use check record for the vacuum, including test label and any defect.
Defect or hazard note for any sticky, wet or unidentified patch found.
Equipment storage check showing mop head position and colour group.
summary: Dry sweeping lifts loose dust; it does not clean grease or residue.
Remove gum and sticky matter first, then sweep with a clean head.
Edges first, then figure-of-eight from the far point back toward the exit.
Store the mop head head up, and check the vacuum before and after use.

knowledgeChecks.question: While sweeping, the mop head picks up a sticky patch. What is the correct response?
options: Keep sweeping, because the head will clean itself once the patch has dried
Stop, remove the sticky matter and fit a clean head before continuing
Dampen the head so it grips the residue and keep sweeping the room

knowledgeChecks.question: Which sweep pattern does this lesson require?
options: Wide arcs across the room, finishing at the window and then along the walls
Straight lines from the door to the far wall and back again each time
Edges first, then figure-of-eight from the far point back toward the exit

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should a mop head be stored between jobs?
options: Face down in a bucket, to keep it damp overnight
Head up in a holder, so it does not collect dirt
On the floor against the wall, to dry out in the open
